title: Review: Reflection and refraction; Mirrors
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W04-ap1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W14-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W14-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W14-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W04-ap1#N.9, W14-1#N.4, W14-2#N.10, W04-ap1#N.1, W14-1#N.9, W14-2#N.9, W14-2#N.4, W14-2#N.8. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Specular reflection
items.clue: Bouncing of light from a smooth surface such as a mirror: parallel in, parallel out, clear image.

items.label: Principal axis
items.clue: Line joining C, which every normal passes through, to the middle of a spherical reflecting surface.

items.label: Focal point
items.clue: Place about R/2 from a curved reflector where reflected parallel rays meet, or appear to come from.

items.label: Virtual image
items.clue: Formed where diverging reflected rays only appear to come from; a screen placed there shows nothing.

questions.stem: A short pulse of light crosses a glass plate (n = 1.50) along the normal to its faces in a time t. The pulse then crosses a diamond plate (n = 2.42) that is twice as thick as the glass plate, also along the normal. How long does the pulse take to cross the diamond plate?

A convex mirror bulges towards the light. Predict before the next screen. A beam of light rays traveling parallel to the principal axis of a convex mirror strikes the mirror. Which statement describes the reflected rays?

options.text: They converge to a point in front of the mirror, where they cross.
They pass through a point behind the mirror, where they cross.
They diverge as if they came from a point behind the mirror.
They go back along their own paths, staying parallel to the axis.

questions.stem: A small object is placed on the principal axis of a concave mirror whose radius of curvature is R. The mirror forms an upright image five times as tall as the object. Use the convention that s_o is positive, s_i is positive for an image in front of the mirror and negative for an image behind it, and f is positive for a concave mirror and negative for a convex mirror. Which expression gives the distance of the object from the mirror?
A narrow laser beam passes through a very narrow slit and then spreads out, making a band of light on a distant screen far wider than the slit. Which explanation of this observation is correct?

options.text: The wave nature of light matters here, and a ray model cannot account for the spreading.
Rays from the slit's two edges fan out along straight lines toward the screen.
Light waves reflect off the edges of the slit, which sends them out to the sides.
Only a few rays can fit through the slit, and they move apart as they travel.

questions.stem: A student walks toward a tall plane mirror, from 3.0 m away to 1.0 m away. How does the height of the student's image at 1.0 m compare with its height at 3.0 m?

options.text: It is greater at 1.0 m, as the image looks bigger from closer up.
It is smaller at 1.0 m, as less of the student fits in the mirror.
Neither has a definite height, as a virtual image is not really there.
They are equal: the image is always as tall as the student.

questions.stem: An object 2.0 cm tall is placed 15.0 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10.0 cm. What is the height of the image?

options.text: 1.0 cm
4.0 cm
2.0 cm
1.3 cm

questions.stem: A convex mirror in a store shows images of customers standing at various distances in front of it. How does the height of each customer's image compare with the customer's height?

options.text: It is larger, as a convex mirror magnifies, like a magnifying glass.
It is smaller, whatever the customer's distance from the mirror.
It is equal, as a mirror forms images the same size as objects.
It is larger for near customers, smaller for those far away.

questions.stem: An object is placed 30.0 cm in front of a convex mirror whose focal length has a magnitude of 20.0 cm. Use the convention that s_o is positive, s_i is positive for an image in front of the mirror and negative for an image behind it, and f is positive for a concave mirror and negative for a convex mirror. What is the image distance s_i?
